title: Strings compare by code point; `FALSE` before `TRUE`
description: Under the default `BINARY` collation `<`, `BETWEEN`, `GREATEST` and `LEAST` order VARCHAR by its UTF-8 bytes, which is code point order (`'\uffff'` is below `'\U0001f600'`, as it is not in UTF-16 order), and BOOLEAN `FALSE < TRUE`. `default_collation` or a column's `COLLATE` changes the order of strings (duckdb-exec-settings, duckdb-string-match-case), so the session stays at the default and a collated column is a different type for the writer.
reference: Strings in code point order (Lean's `String` order, `Value.ltB`); booleans `false < true`; `GREATEST` and `LEAST` skip NULL and keep the first of equal values (`Value.pick`).

provenance.notes: The plans of `s < t`, `s > t`, `s BETWEEN 'a' AND t`, `greatest`, `least` of strings and of booleans give Lean's rows when DuckDB runs the SQL the writer prints, on random rows with NULLs and on rows that separate code point order from UTF-16 order.
